title: pkg/services testing: three coexisting patterns
answers: How are services in pkg/services tested?
Should I use a mock or a real DB in service tests?
What test doubles exist for service interfaces?
body: Three patterns coexist and are chosen per-test: (1) real SQLite via `db.InitTestDB(t)` run against actual migrations, e.g. `pkg/services/star/starimpl/store_test.go:28` — used for store-layer tests. (2) testify/mock against generated mockery mocks (often mocking the k8s/unified-storage client), e.g. `pkg/services/dashboards/service/dashboard_service_test.go` — used for service-layer unit tests with heavier dependencies. (3) Hand-rolled fakes distinct from mockery output, kept in a `*test` subpackage, e.g. `pkg/services/star/startest/fake.go:FakeStarService` — meant for *consumers* of a service that just need a lightweight stand-in, not for testing the service itself.
applies: When writing new tests in pkg/services: test the store layer against a real InitTestDB SQLite instance; test service-layer logic with mockery-generated mocks; when another package merely depends on a service, prefer its existing `*test.FakeX` if present instead of writing a new mock.
